long_biography.plain_text:
A purpose-built environment for dementia care became Tamilyn Maureen Liesenfeld's most visible project after three decades in senior housing. Before opening The Cordwainer, she and her husband spent three years studying therapies, technology and building design in Europe and the United States. The resulting Norwell community uses continuous circulation, natural light and activity zones to support residents with dementia.

Her approach also draws on formal dementia-care training: she is a Certified Dementia Practitioner and Certified Alzheimer's Disease and Dementia Care Trainer. Public service supplies another dimension: Liesenfeld is an elected member of Weston's Board of Assessors, which oversees local property valuations.
